You are writing a plain-language summary of an as-filed Tennessee House bill for an adult reader without legal training.

Use only the bill text supplied in the user message. Treat it as a proposal at introduction, not as proof that it became law or describes current law. Do not use outside knowledge, bill descriptions, later legislative history, or the unstated contents of cited statutes.

Write a neutral summary in prose. Start with what the bill would change. Cover its distinct material provisions, including affected people or organizations, new or changed duties and rights, eligibility rules, amounts and thresholds, deadlines, exceptions, reporting or enforcement requirements, and effective dates when stated. Preserve the bill's conditions and legal distinctions; do not turn a permission into a requirement or a proposal into an enacted rule.

Use familiar words and short, complete sentences. Explain a technical term when the supplied text gives enough context; otherwise retain it rather than guess. Distinguish background or WHEREAS statements from operative provisions, and mention background only when it helps explain the bill. If the bill amends or repeals a cited section without showing that section's contents, describe the textual change and citation without inventing the prior rule or its wider effects.

Keep the summary substantially shorter than the source while retaining the main independent changes. A very short bill may need only one or two sentences; a multi-section bill may need several short paragraphs. Do not add opinions, predicted consequences, a readability score, a confidence rating, headings, bullet points, or a list of citations. Return only the fields required by the supplied output schema.

messages.content:
Bill number: HB0039

<bill_text>
HOUSE BILL 39

 By Davis

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 5;
 Title 6; Title 7; Title 49 and Title 67, relative to the
 Menstrual Hygiene Products Accessibility Act.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-417, is amended by deleting the

section and substituting instead the following:

 (a) This section is known and may be cited as the "Menstrual Hygiene Products

 Accessibility Act."

 (b) As used in this section:

 (1) "Eligible school" means a public school, including a public charter

 school, that is a senior high school, as defined in § 49-6-401; and

 (2) "Feminine hygiene product":

 (A) Means a product or material designed for feminine hygiene in

 connection with menstruation or other genital-tract secretions; and

 (B) Includes tampons, panty liners, menstrual cups, sanitary

 napkins, and other similar personal products or materials.

 (c) Each LEA and public charter school shall provide feminine hygiene products,

 at no charge, in all women's and girls' bathrooms, in all locker rooms, and with the

 school nurse in each eligible school building where instruction is provided, excluding

 bathrooms and locker rooms that are specifically designated for teacher or staff use.

 The feminine hygiene products provided pursuant to this section are for student use

 only.

 (d) The department of education may develop policies and provide guidance to

LEAs and public charter schools to assist local boards of education and public charter

school governing bodies in complying with the requirements of this section.

SECTION 2. This act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

summary.description: Reader-facing plain-language summary in prose, without a heading or bullet points.

summary: This bill would replace Tennessee Code Annotated Section 49-6-417 with a new section called the "Menstrual Hygiene Products Accessibility Act." It would require every local education agency (LEA) and public charter school to provide feminine hygiene products at no charge. The products would be placed in all women's and girls' bathrooms, in all locker rooms, and with the school nurse. This applies in each eligible school building where instruction is provided. An eligible school is a public school, including a public charter school, that is a senior high school as defined in Section 49-6-401. Bathrooms and locker rooms set aside specifically for teachers or staff are excluded. The products would be for student use only. The bill defines feminine hygiene products as products or materials designed for feminine hygiene in connection with menstruation or other genital-tract secretions. This includes tampons, panty liners, menstrual cups, sanitary napkins, and similar personal products. The bill also says the department of education may, but is not required to, develop policies and give guidance to help local boards and charter school governing bodies comply. The bill would take effect July 1, 2025. The title also lists Titles 5, 6, 7, and 67, but the text provided changes only the section in Title 49.
